verdict.line: You lose if you Leap Strike into a fresh Granite Shield or engage while still slowed by Seismic Shard (Q); you win if you strip the shield first and commit Counter Strike (E) only after Brutal Strikes (W) and Ground Slam (E) are both on cooldown.

brief.thesis: This is even on paper (46.7% Jax win rate over 2,132 games) because both champions are combo-reliant rather than poke-reliant: Malphite's Granite Shield passive recharges the moment he isn't being hit, so single pokes waste damage, while Jax's Counter Strike (E) only dodges basic attacks and reduces AoE spell damage - it does not shut down Seismic Shard (Q) or Ground Slam (E) outright. Malphite also has zero gap-close before level 6, so the lane's whole shape is about whether Jax can force sustained auto-trades to break the shield before Ground Slam's attack-speed shred punishes him for trying.

theirWindow.when: Right after his Seismic Shard (Q) lands
theirWindow.what: Seismic Shard steals your movement speed while buffing his, and he can immediately follow with Ground Slam (E) to cut your attack speed - back off rather than trading into this window, since it's built to punish exactly the auto-heavy trade Jax wants.

yourWindow.when: After his W and E both cooldown
yourWindow.what: With Brutal Strikes (14s CD) and Ground Slam (7s CD) both down, Malphite has nothing but autos to answer you - Leap Strike (Q) in, pop Empower (W) on your next hit, and go straight into Counter Strike (E) for the stun.

powerCurve.note: Granite Shield absorbs early poke damage
Ground Slam shreds Jax's attack speed trades
Trinity Force spikes push Jax ahead

start.why: Highest-performing start here (46.5% WR, 1,388 games) - the extra regen and block-on-hit absorb Malphite's constant auto-poke and Seismic Shard chip while you wait for a real all-in window.

boots.why: Best-performing boots (47.8% WR, 1,569 games) - every one of Malphite's damaging abilities (Q, E, R) is magic, so the MR directly reduces his entire kit.

core.why: Core path with 55.5% WR over 164 games; the damage and attack speed feed directly into Relentless Assault's every-third-hit bonus.
Second item on the same measured path - its proc rewards the extended auto-trades you're forced into by Granite Shield.
Closes out the core build and is the only item that lets you survive being caught by Unstoppable Force (R) once he's onto you.

situational.when: malphite pumps armor off repeated Brutal Strikes (W) activations and flat AD stops cutting through him
you're on the Dusk and Dawn path and need sustain to win extended skirmishes rather than burst
you want the hybrid on-hit/ability path instead of Trinity Force for a longer, sustain-heavy lane

runes.keystoneWhy: Highest-performing keystone here (48.1% WR, 24.1% pick) - the heal-on-first-hit and bonus health directly counter Malphite's auto-trade, shield-recharge pattern. Master-tier Jax players instead run Lethal Tempo (Precision, 40.8% WR, 12,515 games) for the attack speed ramp; that suits a more mechanically confident player looking to win extended duels rather than short trades.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the higher measured win rate here (48% vs. Flash+Ignite's 45.9%) - it lets you reset the wave and pick your all-in timing around his shield and cooldowns instead of being forced into a fight before your combo is ready. Flash+Ignite is a viable alt if you want to force a kill the moment his shield is stripped.

playing.title: Bait autos before all-in
playing.detail: Granite Shield recharges the moment Malphite hasn't been hit recently, so throw a couple of autos or an Empower (W) hit to strip it before committing Counter Strike (E) - otherwise your stun combo lands on a shielded target.

playing.title: Don't expect E to no-sell his combo
playing.detail: Counter Strike (E, 18/16/14/12/10s CD) only dodges basic attacks and cuts AoE spell damage - it doesn't block Seismic Shard (Q) or Ground Slam (E) outright, so use it after those are already spent, not as a hard counter to them.

playing.title: Punish after his W and E drop
playing.detail: Brutal Strikes (14s CD) and Ground Slam (7s CD) are his entire trade kit; once both are down he has nothing but autos, so Leap Strike (Q, as low as 5s CD at max rank) in with confidence.

playing.title: Hold Q through his speed steal
playing.detail: Seismic Shard steals your movement speed while buffing his - Leap Strike immediately after it lands means you're slowed while he's fast, so wait for that window to expire before engaging.

playing.title: Treat R as a duel tool, not burst
playing.detail: Relentless Assault has no cooldown but only pays off over extended trades since every third attack deals bonus damage - it doesn't change the math on a short poke exchange against Ground Slam's attack speed shred.

playing.title: Track his ultimate after level 6
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force is 130s at rank 1, down to 80s at ranks 4-5 - after he burns it to engage or peel, you get a long stretch where he has no gap-close beyond walking.

playing.title: Bank toward Zhonya's if the game snowballs
playing.detail: Both measured core paths end on Zhonya's Hourglass - if Malphite's team gets ahead and starts hunting you in skirmishes, prioritize it earlier than the standard build order.

brief.patchCaveat: The win rates, build order, runes, and summoners above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the timing windows and ability interactions are my own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Malphite’s Ground Slam (E) reduces your attack speed. Even if you execute your Leap Strike [Q] - Counter Strike [E] combo, his Ground Slam (E) – Seismic Shard (Q) combo will deal more damage. Try to use Leap Strike [Q] when his speed buff from Seismic Shard (Q) ends.
